svg.title: ACC32-HARV
svg.desc: ACC32-HARV fixed 32-bit instruction format chosen for this schematic. Every instruction occupies four bytes in byte-addressed IM; IM returns one 32-bit instruction word. Absolute: opcode[31:24], operand[23:0]. Relative: opcode[31:24], reserved[23:16], offset[15:0]. IR latches IWORD[31:24]; OP is a 24-bit register and latches IWORD[23:0] in the same fetch cycle. OP has one output bus, which forks to SX16 (low 16 bits, sign bit 15) and SX24 (all 24 bits, sign bit 23). Each SX is fixed wiring for sign extension to 32 bits. There is no direct OP bypass, byte assembly, byte write enable, or OP clear. AC has one 32-bit output bus, branching outside the register to the ALU A mux and the memory/I/O write-data interface. ALU A selects PC or AC; ALU B selects rdata, SX16 or SX24. The B mux inputs from top to bottom are rdata=0, SX16=1, SX24=2. PC remains at the current instruction until completion. Relative addressing uses AR=PC+SX16(OP) in one ALU operation. Normal completion advances PC by a fixed +4 incrementer; taken absolute branches select the ALU PASS B result SX24(OP) instead. HALT holds PC. The AR-to-ALU feedback and the constant 3 are absent. Absolute address formation uses AR=SX24(OP); load_acc uses AR=AC. store_ind execution after fetch: AR=SX24(OP), then AR=MEM32[AR] through read MUX and ALU PASS B, then MEM32[AR]=AC and PC=PC+4. AR output drives the shared data address interface and address decoder only. One main ALU; Harvard IM and DM are separate. CU is an opaque hardwired control block with internal instruction sequencing and branch predicates. ALU and its attached N/Z/V/C cells form one functional unit. Flags are formed internally from the ALU operation: N is result bit 31, Z tests the 32-bit result for zero, and V/C come from the operation's overflow/carry logic. There is no separate AC-to-flags connection or external flag-generation circuit. N/Z latch when an ALU result is committed to AC, so address calculations do not overwrite accumulator condition flags. The four-bit flag output feeds CU. Flag update/clear control is implicit. V/C update only for ADD/SUB/MUL or explicit clear; address calculations, fetch, loads and stores preserve them. Memory and devices share addr/wdata/rdata/rd/wr; DEC gates DM, input data register ID at 0x80, output data register OD at 0x84 and Read MUX selection. MMIO addresses are excluded from DM. Reads are combinational; writes and I/O side effects occur once at a clock edge. All data/address paths are 32 bit except the labelled instruction fields and OP bus. This requested fixed-length hardware encoding differs from Wrench 0.0.5.0 variable-length encoding; see acc32-harv-notes.md. Dots indicate junctions or labelled bit-field taps; bridges indicate unconnected crossings.
